findings.description: The 'data' bucket sets no ACL restriction and has no public access block, and the inline comment confirms it is intended to be public. Anyone on the internet could list and read objects, including the customer master file uploaded to it.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so sensitive customer data stored in this bucket is not encrypted with SSE-KMS at rest.
The bucket has no logging block, so unauthorized access to this public bucket containing customer data would leave no audit trail.
There is no bucket policy denying non-HTTPS (aws:SecureTransport = false) requests, so objects may be transmitted in cleartext.
A customer master spreadsheet is uploaded into the publicly accessible, unencrypted 'data' bucket with no per-object encryption (kms_key_id) specified, exposing sensitive customer records.
The financials bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving financial data unencrypted at rest.
No logging block is configured, so access to financial data cannot be audited or investigated after a compromise.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a future ACL or bucket policy change could silently make financial data public.
The operations bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so its contents are stored without enforced SSE-KMS encryption.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, removing the audit trail needed to detect unauthorized object access.
No public access block is attached, so account- or bucket-level ACL/policy changes could expose the bucket publicly without an enforced guardrail.
The data science bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving potentially sensitive datasets unencrypted at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource protects this bucket, so its private ACL is the only barrier to public exposure.
The log archive bucket has no public access block; log data often contains sensitive request metadata and should be explicitly shielded from public ACLs and policies.

findings.issue_category: missing access logging on log bucket
findings.description: The central log bucket itself has no logging configuration, so tampering with or exfiltration of audit logs would go unrecorded.
